text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Latvian society of tenants organised on November 2 a rally in the centre of Riga to protest against the government's plans to abolish a ceiling to rents.

- Russian deputy foreign minister Sergei Krylov announced that Russia is not considering the introduction of economic sanctions against Latvia but he believes Russia should shift its cargo flow from Latvian harbours to its own ports.
- Finance Ministry state secretary Valentina Andrejeva announced plans to reorganise the ministry and a 10 percent reduction of its personnel in the next two to three years.

- During his meeting with officials of the Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA), Prime Minister Andris Shkele said that at least 15 percent or $1.5 billion worth of shares in major state-owned companies should be sold for privatisation vouchers.
- Lattelekom, owned jointly by Cable and Wireless and Telecom Finland, has opened a fibre optic cable to Belarus.
- Latvenergo, the state energy supplier up for sale, plans to revalue its assets next year.
